components.css: .ds-symptom{position:relative;display:inline-flex;cursor:pointer}.ds-symptom input{position:absolute;opacity:0;inset:0}.ds-symptom span{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;min-height:42px;padding:7px 13px;border:1px solid #8a9893;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:var(--ink,#17252b);font:400 16px/1.35 PlexThai,'Noto Sans Thai',sans-serif}.ds-symptom:hover span{border-color:var(--green,#277a64)}.ds-symptom input:checked+span{border-color:var(--ink,#17252b);background:var(--ink,#17252b);color:#fff}.ds-symptom input:focus-visible+span{outline:3px solid var(--green,#277a64);outline-offset:3px}

narrative.overview: The selected road-sign and road-line direction makes each report feel like a short, legible route from a numbered pole to a finished repair. The visual language pairs high-contrast road ink with warm light surfaces and restrained sign yellow. A lightbulb mark remains the brand anchor. The public form gives the pole number the strongest field treatment and pairs it with a dark three-step route panel. Staff screens use the same palette at a denser pace: rail navigation, thin dividers, compact metrics, rows, and status pills keep work scannable.
keyCharacteristics: Thai-first IBM Plex Sans Thai with large, clear pole numbers and tabular numeric status data.
Yellow reserved for brand, main actions, active tabs, and route markings.
Cream canvas, off-white working surfaces, dark ink, and status colors with textual labels.
Dashed road markings and numbered route circles used as recurring cues.

rules.name: The Sign Accent Rule
rules.body: Yellow identifies a route or a primary action; keep ordinary body text in road ink.

rules.name: The Number First Rule
rules.body: Give pole identifiers and status counts immediate visual priority before decorative road cues.

rules.name: The Quiet Workspace Rule
rules.body: Use lines and surface color to separate routine staff data; reserve lifting shadows for prominent or interactive surfaces.

dos: Do lead a public reporting flow with the pole number and one clear yellow submit action.
Do keep status words visible with their colored dots.
Do preserve the lightbulb, sign yellow, and dashed route cue across public and staff surfaces.
Do keep staff data compact enough to scan while retaining readable labels on mobile.
donts: Don't spread warning colors or dashed markings across routine content; the selected direction treats them as purposeful cues.
Don't rely on color alone for progress, selection, or errors.
Don't replace clear pole and status labels with decorative road graphics.
